answer:
**Short answer:** Casual leave is deducted day-for-day from your accrued balance when you take it, but **casual leave cannot be encashed at all** — so an "encashment" of casual leave days is not a permitted transaction and would not reduce your casual leave balance. Only Earned/Privilege Leave can be encashed (up to 5 days at year end).

## 1. How casual leave is deducted when you take leave

- Casual Leave accrues at **1 day per completed month of service, up to 12 days per calendar year**, and the balance is visible in the HRMS at the start of each month [leave_policy § 3.1 Accrual and Usage].
- You may use it as soon as it has accrued; **advancing usage against future accrual is not permitted** [leave_policy § 3.1 Accrual and Usage]. So a day taken is deducted from the balance already accrued — you cannot go negative.
- Requests must go through the HRMS portal (email/chat requests are not formally submitted); planned leave needs advance notice, and unplanned leave must be reported before 10:00 AM and regularized in the HRMS within 2 working days [leave_policy § 3.3 Application Procedure]. The 2025 amendment reduced the planned-leave notice from 2 working days to **1 working day** effective July 1, 2025 [leave_policy_2025_amendment § Leave Policy Amendment — 2025 (Policy CL-2025-07)].
- Probationary employees are capped at 1 casual leave day per month [leave_policy § 1. Overview].

## 2. Encashment — casual leave is excluded

- Unused casual leave above the carry-forward cap "lapses permanently on December 31 and **cannot be recovered, encashed, or transferred to another leave type**" [leave_policy § 3.2 Carry-Forward].
- The only encashment provision in the policy is for **Earned/Privilege Leave: "Up to 5 unused days may be encashed at year end"** [leave_policy § 2. Leave Types and Annual Entitlements].

So if the 2 days in your scenario are casual leave, the documents do not permit encashing them, and no deduction from the casual leave balance occurs on that account. If they are Earned/Privilege Leave days, they come out of that separate 18-day balance, not the casual leave balance [leave_policy § 2. Leave Types and Annual Entitlements].

## 3. The resulting balance

Using your figures — 14 days casual leave balance, 3 days taken, 2 days encashed:

- Leave taken: **14 − 3 = 11 days** remaining.
- Encashment: **no deduction**, because casual leave cannot be encashed [leave_policy § 3.2 Carry-Forward].
- **Resulting casual leave balance: 11 days** (14 − 3 = 11; the 2 encashed days are not deducted from casual leave).

That 11 is my arithmetic on your inputs, not a figure stated in any passage.

## 4. Two things to check against your own numbers

**a) A 14-day casual leave balance is not a standard annual entitlement.** The annual entitlement is 12 days [leave_policy § 2. Leave Types and Annual Entitlements]. A 14-day balance could only arise through carry-forward from the previous year.

**b) The carry-forward cap is itself disputed.** The base policy caps carry-forward at **6 days** [leave_policy § 3.2 Carry-Forward], while the 2025 amendment states the cap "is increased from 6 days to **15 days**" effective July 1, 2025 [leave_policy_2025_amendment § Leave Policy Amendment — 2025 (Policy CL-2025-07)]. The contradiction scanner has flagged these two passages as an open, verified conflict [contradiction #2]. The amendment is dated and expressly amends § 3.2, but the documents do not contain a clause stating which text governs the unamended policy document, so I am reporting both rather than picking one. This matters for your balance: under a 6-day cap, days above 6 would lapse on December 31; under a 15-day cap, up to 15 would carry forward.

**Not covered:** the documents do not describe the payroll mechanics of encashment (rate of pay, timing of payment) for Earned/Privilege Leave beyond the 5-day year-end limit.

Sources:
- [leave_policy § 3.1 Accrual and Usage]
- [leave_policy § 3.2 Carry-Forward]
- [leave_policy § 3.3 Application Procedure]
- [leave_policy § 2. Leave Types and Annual Entitlements]
- [leave_policy § 1. Overview]
- [leave_policy_2025_amendment § Leave Policy Amendment — 2025 (Policy CL-2025-07)]
- Contradiction flag #2 (OPEN, verified)
